qs.e: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone is secreted by the hypothalamus to stimulate the release of both FSH and LH.

ai.subject: Biochemistry & genetics
ai.summary: Hypothalamic hormones are key regulators of the anterior pituitary, controlling endocrine cascades that affect growth, reproduction, and metabolism. They act as releasing or inhibiting signals, and their dysregulation leads to common endocrine disorders.

sections.p: The hypothalamus releases peptides that either stimulate or inhibit anterior pituitary hormones. This central control ensures coordinated endocrine responses to physiological needs.
Neurons in the hypothalamus synthesize hormones, store them in axon terminals, and release them into portal vessels that carry them to the pituitary.
b: Releasing hormones bind pituitary receptors to trigger hormone secretion
Inhibitory hormones bind receptors to suppress secretion

sections.p: Target organ hormones (e.g., thyroid hormone, cortisol) provide negative feedback to the hypothalamus, adjusting releasing hormone secretion.

t.b: High TSH → hypothyroidism; low TSH → hyperthyroidism

sections.p: Imbalance of releasing or inhibiting hormones causes endocrine disorders such as hyperprolactinemia, hypothyroidism, or growth hormone excess.

t.b: Elevated prolactin → pituitary adenoma or hypothyroidism

sections.p: Recognizing patterns of pituitary hormone excess or deficiency guides diagnosis of common endocrine diseases and informs treatment choices.
b: Hypothyroidism presents with fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance

t.b: Elevated TSH with low free T4 → primary hypothyroidism
Low LH/FSH with low estradiol → hypogonadotropic hypogonadism

sections.p: Remember the four classic releasing hormones and their target pituitary hormones. In low-resource settings, clinical clues often outweigh laboratory confirmation.

whenToSeekHelp: Severe hyperprolactinemia with visual field loss (possible pituitary macroadenoma)
Unexplained severe hypothyroidism with cardiac symptoms
